### Day 248: Acts 14:21–22
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-248-acts-14-2122.html
Passage: Acts 14:21-22
Points:
- Paul and Barnabas risked danger to backtrack through hostile cities specifically to strengthen and encourage young believers.
- Telling disciples that hardships are inevitable sounds counterintuitive, but facing that reality prevents wasted energy on fear.
- Acknowledging the certainty of tribulations allows believers to focus on remaining faithful rather than avoiding difficulty.
- Enduring trials is a normal part of kingdom life rather than proof of spiritual failure, immaturity, or disobedience.

### Mission Accomplished - Today's Insight - July 20, 2024
Author: Charles Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/todays-insight-july-20-2024.html
Passage: Acts 14:21-23
Points:
- Paul and Barnabas retraced their steps to encourage converts and establish church leadership without nursing grievances or regrets over past mistreatment.
- Their single-minded focus remained on pursuing genuine ministry that honored God above all else.
- When delivering their report in Antioch, they attributed every success and open door among the Gentiles entirely to God's work.
- Christian servants must embrace their responsibilities while ensuring all praise and credit belong to the Lord alone.
